title: LoRA Superposition across Pretrained Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.30691v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is usually tied to the pretrained backbone on which it is learned. We ask whether LoRAs trained independently for the same task on different pretrained backbones can be summed and applied unchanged to all contributing backbones. We call this construction LoRA superposition. Across seven ViT-B/16 CLIP backbones and eight image-classification tasks, the exact sum improves all 56 backbone-task pairs and achieves a mean accuracy gain of 30.21 percentage points over the unadapted backbone. The exact sum achieves a mean accuracy only 0.28 percentage points below that of individually trained solo LoRAs. In contrast, a leave-one-model-out (LOMO) sum produces a mean gain of only 0.06 percentage points over the unadapted backbones. tldr: 该论文提出“LoRA叠加”概念，证明在不同预训练骨干网络上针对同一任务独立训练的LoRA可以直接相加并无修改地应用于所有骨干网络，其效果接近单独训练的LoRA，平均准确率提升高达30.21个百分点。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces "LoRA superposition," showing that LoRAs independently trained on different pretrained backbones for the same task can be summed and applied unchanged to all backbones, achieving accuracy gains of 30.21 percentage points on average—nearly matching individually trained LoRAs.
